story: Gary is sorting clamps and mounting hardware at his house, tucking his wiring sketches neatly in while he waits, hopeful, for approval on his project. Donna is cheerfully texting Gary to confirm their one o'clock meeting at the court and to remind him about the 6 PM cart parade. Hal is determinedly heading out along Magnolia Loop on a Saturday morning in the warm 81-degree sunshine. Meanwhile, Rosa is pulling the last tray from her kitchen oven, bagging the final Halloween treats, and stacking them by her door.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Sort the clamps and mounting hardware and tuck the wiring sketches in, ready for approval
Donna (donna phone): Text Gary to confirm one o'clock at the court and remind him of the 6 PM cart parade
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Pull the last tray out, finish bagging the Halloween treats, and stack them by the door

gary.thought_process: It's Halloween morning and the parade is at 6 tonight. My Architectural Review application still isn't signed off, and L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need approval, so nothing gets mounted on the cart. I've bench-tested the wiring and untangled the light strings. Best use of this hour is to organize the clamp list and wiring sketches in the toolbox so everything's ready to mount the moment approval comes through. I could also go check on the application, but I already did that at the review desk and don't want to nag.

parameters.content: Sort the clamps and mounting hardware and tuck the wiring sketches in, ready for approval

donna.thought_process: I've already checked the club calendar and my pickleball bag, so I'm set for the one o'clock court time with Gary. It's only 9:17 and nobody is around. The phone is the one thing left in the house, and a quick text to Gary confirming one o'clock and my Halloween parade plans keeps the day moving without repeating what I said at tick 211. After that I can head out to the Loop and see the pumpkins.

parameters.content: Text Gary to confirm one o'clock at the court and remind him of the 6 PM cart parade

hal.thought_process: I scanned the Loop and logged the counts last tick, but I'm still sitting at home with a notebook full of numbers and nobody to show them to. My goal is to get Gary's cart mods and Donna's flamingos in front of the architectural review committee, and that means going out and doing it properly rather than grumbling on the porch. Halloween's parade is tonight, so the street will fill up with carts and decorations by evening. Best to head out to Magnolia Loop now, verify what I recorded with my own eyes, and keep everything fair and by the book.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop with my notebook to verify the flamingo and cart counts before the parade crowds show up.

rosa.thought_process: I'm home, nobody's nearby, and the schedule check is done, so Saturday evening is clear. I've been baking and bagging treats for two ticks now, and the town news says pumpkins are going up on porches. The last thing I did was keep baking, so the batch should be nearly done. The best move is to wrap up the treat bagging so I'm ready for the trick-or-treaters tonight and can head out to the Loop to see Gary and Donna.

parameters.content: Pull the last tray out, finish bagging the Halloween treats, and stack them by the door

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
